# omadafusion_lan_network_dhcp_dns (Resource)

Manages only the DNS servers that an existing LAN network's DHCP server hands out. The network itself is not created or deleted. Every other network field is read and sent back unchanged.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "omadafusion_lan_network" "staff" {
  name = "Staff"
}

resource "omadafusion_lan_network_dhcp_dns" "staff" {
  network_id    = data.omadafusion_lan_network.staff.id
  primary_dns   = "1.1.1.1"
  secondary_dns = "1.0.0.1"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `network_id` (String) LAN network ID.

### Optional

- `primary_dns` (String) Primary DNS server handed out by DHCP. Leave both DNS attributes unset to hand out the gateway (`auto`).
- `reset_on_destroy` (Boolean) On destroy, set the network back to handing out the gateway (`auto`). Defaults to `true`.
- `secondary_dns` (String) Secondary DNS server.
- `site` (String) Site name or ID. Defaults to the provider `site`. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as `network_id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <network_id> or <site>/<network_id>
terraform import omadafusion_lan_network_dhcp_dns.staff Default/64f0c0ffee00000000000001
```
